name: Workflow Builder (design → author → register)
description: A meta-workflow that builds new workflows. Give it a goal and a new workflow id; it designs the pipeline, authors a schema-valid template, then registers it via the Cowork API so it is immediately runnable — no hand-editing of workflows/*.json.

steps.title: Design the "{{workflow_id}}" pipeline
Author the "{{workflow_id}}" template JSON
steps.description:
Turn the approved design into a single valid Cowork workflow definition JSON and save it to the artifacts dir as `workflow.json`. It MUST conform to this schema:

{
  "id": "{{workflow_id}}",            // kebab-case; this is the template's stable id
  "name": "<human label>",
  "description": "<one-liner>",
  "mode": "dag" | "orchestrated",   // omit for dag
  "goal": "<orchestrated mode only>",
  "params": ["<name>", ...],          // referenced as {{name}} in titles/descriptions
  "steps": [
    { "key": "<unique kebab-case>", "title": "...", "description": "...",
      "division": "<optional>", "agent": "<optional>", "brain": "<optional>",
      "priority": "low|normal|high|urgent", "dependsOn": ["<earlier step key>"] }
  ]
}

Rules the validator enforces: every step needs a unique string `key`; every `dependsOn` entry must reference an existing step key; the graph must be acyclic (no step may transitively depend on itself). Write ONLY the JSON object to workflow.json (no prose, no markdown fences) so it can be registered as-is.

steps.title: Register + verify the "{{workflow_id}}" workflow
steps.description:
Register the authored template with the Cowork server so it becomes runnable. POST the contents of workflow.json to the Cowork API:

  curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:6868/api/workflows \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d @workflow.json

A 201 with { ok: true, workflow: {...} } means it validated and was written to workflows/{{workflow_id}}.json. If you get "already exists", re-POST with the body wrapped as {"def": <the json>, "overwrite": true}. Then verify it loads and expands correctly with a dry run:

  curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:6868/api/workflows/{{workflow_id}}/run \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"dryRun": true, "params": {}}'

(fill the params object with sample values for the template's params). Report the registration response and the resolved dry-run step list. If the host running this step cannot reach the Cowork API, say so plainly and leave workflow.json as the deliverable for a host that can register it — do not fake a success.
